cards.headline: Black 9 takes a ko, but Black lives whatever White does: S[KO+] by your practice, S[ALIVE] as the research reads it. The tree's S[ADKO] is wrong either way.

diagrams.caption: The tree's line to the leaf, marked S[ADKO]; the solver prints KO+. Black 9 captures White's stone at D18, so White may not retake there at once. White to play.

White 10 retakes after a ko threat elsewhere, and Black 11 connects instead of fighting the ko. After White 12 and Black 13, White's corner stones and White 10 have one liberty, at D19. White 14 fills an outside liberty, but Black still has two, and Black 15 captures five stones.
If White 12 connects at D19 instead, Black 13 puts White's stones at A19 and B18 in atari. After White 14, Black 15 takes them: two eyes, at A19 and B18.

text: In Diagram 1 White may not retake at D18 at once, and White's corner stones are short of liberties: White 2 and White 4 are in atari, and White 6 and White 8 each have only A18 and B19. White's only real try is to retake at D18 after a threat (Diagram 2). Black does not fight the ko: Black 11 joins all of Black's stones, with four liberties, and White runs out of liberties first. If White 12 connects at D19 instead (Diagram 3), Black takes two stones and has two eyes.

So Black lives without a ko capture of its own, even against unlimited White threats; in both search areas every White move at the leaf fails. Yet the line ends with Black's capture of a ko, the case of the question above. By your practice such a leaf is S[KO+], and the solver follows it and prints KO+; the research reads it by its clean status, S[ALIVE]. Both answers agree on the play; they differ in the label, and so in what the site accepts.

The tree's S[ADKO] fits neither answer: it means Black lives only through a double ko. The leaf has two ko shapes, at D18 and at B19, which probably explains the label, but Black needs neither. Either answer changes the site's grading and needs moves added to the tree, and those wait for the site's ko-threat moves (Change the tree as well, below).

Both answers wait for the site's ko-threat moves. Each needs White 8 in Diagram 1, a retake at C17 after a ko threat elsewhere that Black answers, and the tree cannot hold that exchange yet; you are building the system for it. Until then leave 11332 as it is: without White 8, either new S[] makes the site reject a good move (On the site, below). Two passes standing in for the threat and its answer would not grade right: Black's best answer to White's pass is to connect at C17, which lives outright.

With S[ALIVE] on the leaf, add White 8. The leaf shows that the tree's only answer to Black's C18 at move 7, at a, is a mistake; without White 8, besogo thinks C18 lives outright and rejects Black's A18 at move 7. The retake is White's best answer: every other White move lets Black live outright. Black 9 in Diagram 2 then transposes to the tree's A18 at move 7 and its double ko, so White 8 gets S[ADKO], decided in the narrow search area only; besogo links the transposition itself. Black 9 in Diagram 3 is optional.

With S[KO+] on the leaf, besogo ranks Black's D19 at move 9 below the double ko after Black's A18 there, so the site rejects D19 and keeps A18. Adding Black 9 in Diagram 3 with S[ALIVE] changes that: the site then accepts only that move there, the clean one, as your practice intends. But then besogo again thinks C18 at move 7 lives outright, through the tree's answer at a, and rejects Black's A18 at move 7, so White 8 is required as well.
The checker's tree reader will need to read the new exchange too; today it drops an immediate ko retake without a warning.

diagrams.caption: Required under either answer. After Black's C18 at move 7, add White 8, retaking at C17 after a ko threat elsewhere that Black answers, as a second answer beside the tree's answer at a, and put S[ADKO] on White 8.

Why S[ADKO]: Black 9 gives the position after the tree's A18 at move 7, with White to play, and White 10 and Black 11 reach that line's leaf, marked S[ADKO]. besogo links the transposition by itself; adding this whole line grades the same.

Black 9 lives as well as the tree's D19 (solver: ALIVE in both search areas); add it with S[ALIVE]. Optional with S[ALIVE] on the leaf, where besogo marks both correct; required with S[KO+], where the site then accepts only Black 9.

text: With S[ALIVE] on the leaf alone, the problem's result goes from S[ADKO] to S[ALIVE], and the site marks a wrong in Diagrams 1 and 2, with the two moves after each; today both are correct. The grading check found the new result and the mark in Diagram 1 wrong, and the mark in Diagram 2 right. With White's retake at C17 added (Change the tree as well, above), besogo's own grading keeps the problem at S[ADKO] and a and b in Diagram 1 correct; only a in Diagram 2 and the two moves after it turn wrong.

Diagram 1: a and b are equally good: after b, White's best answer is to retake at C17 after a threat, which leads to the same double ko as a (Change the tree as well, above). The tree has only White's A19 after b, which the leaf shows to be a mistake, so with S[ALIVE] besogo thinks b lives outright, marks a wrong and raises the problem to ALIVE. These move-7 results are decided in the narrow search area only; the wider one stayed undecided even at 2,000,000 nodes.

Diagram 2: after White 8, b lives outright, as the leaf shows, and c lives as well. Move a lets White 10 retake at C17, and Black gets only the double ko of the tree's leaf (Diagram 3). ALIVE ranks above ADKO, so with S[ALIVE] a is a real mistake.

With S[KO+] on the leaf alone, the problem stays S[ADKO], but besogo ranks b in Diagram 2 below a and marks b wrong: not right, since b lives outright. With c added as S[ALIVE], the site accepts only c, as your practice intends, but it marks a in Diagram 1 wrong and calls the problem ALIVE unless White's retake is added too.

diagrams.caption: Black to play move 7. Today a and b are both correct, each worth S[ADKO]. With S[ALIVE] on the leaf but no White retake at C17, the site marks a wrong and calls the problem ALIVE. Not right: a and b lead to the same double ko.

Black to play move 9, after b in Diagram 1 and the tree's White 8. Today a and b are both correct, and c is not in the tree. With S[ALIVE] the site marks a wrong and keeps b, the leaf: right. With S[KO+] alone it marks b wrong and keeps a: not right.
The tree's line for a in Diagram 2, marked S[ADKO]. White 10 retakes at C17, and Black 11 takes White 8: Black gets only a double ko, while b lives outright.
